- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.10) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +3–5% above prior high or use 30-day moving average as anchor.
- If sentiment turns positive (avg > 0.10) after a downtrend, model often underreacts; increase forecast by 1–3% to reflect sentiment momentum.
- Model frequently overestimates early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile; apply 10–15% downward bias if sentiment swings >0.20 in last 5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast > 80 and true outcome drops below 75, model often fails to adjust; apply 5–10% downward correction if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- Lagged response: if true outcome is below 70 for 3+ consecutive days, model often misses the drop; adjust forecast to align with 10-day moving average of true values.
